solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Material gain is wrongly distributed — this political outlook demands greater fairness?

definitions.text: this political outlook demands greater fairness?

indicators.note: letters handed out in the wrong way end up in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone complains that material gain is shared out unjustly, and names the creed that would put it right.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine of equal rights and opportunity for all is a political outlook that presses for fairness.

clue.text: Excessive size makes man sit awkwardly, having joined carriage

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: placed awkwardly, these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A big man squeezes clumsily into a cramped railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' suggests a train, but here it is the horse-drawn kind; 'awkwardly' makes ANTISM, and 'having joined' simply attaches it.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term is for abnormal overgrowth of the body, so it is excessive size.

clue.text: Everyone climbing? No: the land is flat here

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: everyone means all
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether everyone is going up a hill and is told no, because the ground here is flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ALL into LLA in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless plain of South America, a place where the terrain is level.

clue.text: Dangerous driver's excessively lax initially — it could be lethal

parts.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is a notoriously reckless motorist, so the driver's is TOAD'S
excessively means too

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word lax

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist is far too casual, and the result could kill someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad is the car-mad hero of Kenneth Grahame's children's book; his possessive gives TOADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Many fungi of this kind are poisonous, so one could kill whoever eats it.

clue.text: Tricks and exploits overseen by king

indicators.note: in a down entry, being overseen by means sitting below, so the king's letter comes on top

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)
to exploit something is to use it, so exploits means uses

explanation.surface: A monarch supervises schemes and daring deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are cunning stratagems, the sort of tricks used to deceive.

clue.text: Plentiful gain wickedly acquired — certain to get hidden

indicators.note: the scrambled gain takes in another piece, which it thus acquires
the second piece gets hidden by being placed within the first
used wickedly, the letters of gain are twisted into another order

parts.note: bound, as in bound to happen, means certain

explanation.surface: Riches gained by crooked means are bound to be stashed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' makes AING; 'acquired' and 'to get hidden' both say the second piece sits within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abounding exists in great quantity, which is what plentiful means.

clue.text: Home help set up in the country

parts.note: to be home is to be in

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the word is raised, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: help means aid

explanation.surface: A domestic helper is installed in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns AID into DIA beneath IN.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation of South Asia, so it fits a clue asking for a country.

clue.text: I'm ready to work when the sun is at its highest

definitions.text: when the sun is at its highest

indicators.note: letters put to work are reshaped, so these get rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker announces they are set to start the day's labour at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: In midsummer, around the middle of the calendar in the northern hemisphere, the sun climbs highest.

clue.text: Gosh — that's the least you could offer anyone!

definitions.text: that's the least you could offer anyone!
definitions.meaning: tiny scraps from a loaf, the smallest thing one could hand over

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise followed by a remark on the stingiest offering imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a mild British exclamation of dismay and the small fragments left from bread.

clue.text: Newspaper has good article on modern music

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A paper runs a decent feature on contemporary music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a style of dance music from Jamaica, related to reggae and dancehall, dating from the 1980s.

clue.text: Sailor temporarily assigned (not English) did a bunk

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: not means the following letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a worker seconded is temporarily transferred to other duties

explanation.surface: A seaman on a temporary posting abroad deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: One E goes from SECONDED, leaving SCONDED. 'Did a bunk' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a bunk is to flee secretly, as one who has absconded has done.

clue.text: Fellow disappears in fruit trees

parts.note: a fellow is a man
something that disappears goes, as in 'the pain goes'

explanation.surface: A man vanishes into an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the tropical fruit and the evergreen trees that bear it.

clue.text: Seasonal visitor felt half abandoned in US city

parts.note: Father Christmas visits at Christmas time

indicators.note: the back half of the word felt is left behind, keeping only its first two letters

explanation.surface: Father Christmas feels rather neglected on a trip to an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital of New Mexico, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Formal society having difference of opinion

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A starchy club falls into a squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are stilted and ceremonious, so the word fits formal behaviour.

clue.text: Financial activity that keeps someone's head above water?

definitions.meaning: a company launching its shares on the stock market

definitions.text: that keeps someone's head above water?
definitions.meaning: the act or means of staying buoyant in water

explanation.surface: A money-market manoeuvre that saves someone from drowning in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a stock-market launch of a company and keeping something afloat; 'head above water' is also an idiom for staying solvent.

clue.text: It's unlikely one would provide tot with fur tie!

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement of these letters gives something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clothier would hardly kit a toddler out with a fur necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of TOT, FUR and TIE; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop supplying clothes and equipment is one that would provide such an outfit.

clue.text: You'll see rector win converts — someone proclaiming an important message

indicators.note: a convert changes form, so these letters change into another order

explanation.surface: A churchman gains converts and spreads important news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for new believers but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In old towns an official rang a bell and shouted public announcements in the streets.

clue.text: Fascinating article about small flower

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
a flower is something that flows, a river, and a small one is a rill, a brook

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a little bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks grammatical (A, THE) but is THING; 'flower' is the crossword's flowing thing, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fascinating excites and grips you, which is what a thrilling thing does.

clue.text: Like a matchless partner?

parts.note: a match is a marriage, so a partner without one lives together unwed

explanation.surface: Praise for a peerless companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matchless' seems to mean unequalled but here means without a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A common-law wife or husband is a partner treated as a spouse though never formally married.

clue.text: Risks taken by Dutch ancestors

indicators.note: the answer is taken by, held within, the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Gambles made by forebears from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To take chances is to take risks, so the two plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: King entering biblical city courtyard

indicators.note: entering means this letter goes into the next piece

parts.note: Gath was a Philistine city, home of Goliath
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A monarch rides into an ancient city's courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an old word for an enclosed yard or garden, especially a cloister's.

clue.text: Men in Berlin sin, being in the clutches of female

indicators.note: something in another's clutches is held inside it

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, and slang for a woman
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: Men in the German capital go astray while gripped by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Herren is the German word for gentlemen, used by people in Berlin.

clue.text: Very old piece of furniture shortened to fit into car somehow

indicators.note: the shortened piece is made to fit inside the next one
rearranged somehow, the letters of car come out in another order
shortened means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a chair is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone tries to squeeze a cut-down antique seat into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator turns the vehicle's letters into ARC; 'shortened' docks the seat's last letter, and the result fits between ARC's R and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to an earlier era, antiquated.

clue.text: Top commander entertaining artist to have a good time in Dublin?

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: C-in-C, CIC, is Commander-in-Chief
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A general hosts a painter to enjoy themselves in the Irish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Craic is Irish for fun, lively company and conversation, so it is enjoyment as Dubliners say it.

clue.text: Church member making appeal

parts.note: a member is a limb, such as an arm

explanation.surface: A churchgoer makes a plea for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is attractiveness, the power to please, which is the noun appeal.

clue.text: Last person to do a repair job?

definitions.text: Last person to do a repair job?

parts.words: Last person to do a repair job?
parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block on which shoes are mended, so a last person is one who works on it

explanation.surface: Asking who would be the final choice to fix something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like 'final' but is the shoe-repairer's block.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes, using a last to hold them.

clue.text: After onset of biliousness suspend drug

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the first one
the onset is the beginning, so this takes the opening letter

parts.note: to suspend is to hang

explanation.surface: A queasy patient is told to stop taking a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhang is a preparation of cannabis used in India, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Tea with one Indian musician coming back for a noisy celebration

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: coming back means these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ravi Shankar was the famous Indian sitar player

explanation.surface: A sitarist returns to take tea with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the one and the musician into IVARI. Char is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a cacophonous mock serenade, raucous revelry, often for newlyweds.

clue.text: Nibblers getting at a garment

indicators.note: the nibblers get at, come up to, the letter, so they follow it

parts.note: mice nibble things

explanation.surface: Rodents are chewing a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a white linen cloth worn on the neck and shoulders by a priest, a liturgical vestment.

clue.text: Good Germans etc involved in additional accommodation expense

indicators.note: letters involved are entangled, so these get mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Decent Germans and others get caught up in an extra housing cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A further loan secured on a home is an extra cost of housing.
